subject: Aequitas debug log retention exception & evidence request
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aequitashealth.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: Security Team <security@aequitashealth.com>, Aequitas Procurement <procure@aequitashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tenant-scoped debug log retention beyond standard TTL

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick call earlier. We are kicking off a formal ask so our internal compliance team has the artifacts they need. As discussed, Aequitas is in the middle of a regulatory review for a small subset of transactions tied to one clinical partner. To support the review we need debug session traces and request/response logs scoped to tenant ID AEQ-237 for 180 days instead of Redwood's default 30-day debug TTL.

Specific asks:
- Confirm whether Redwood can make a tenant-scoped exception to retain debug/session logs for AEQ-237 for 180 days.
- Provide a list of artifacts/proofs you can deliver to satisfy our security and audit teams (SOC 2, SIG, CAIQ): retention matrix, proof-of-delete API details, sample redacted logs, and a documented approval workflow.
- If a written amendment (DPA/SOW) or signed attestation is required, please confirm the lead time and point of contact for DocuSign.

We're happy to accept redacted samples and system attestations rather than full PII-bearing data. Please copy procurement for commercial/contract coordination.

Regards,
Samir
Samir Patel
Sr. Security Engineer | Aequitas Health
attachments: aequitas_scope.csv (stub)

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aequitashealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Aequitas Procurement <procure@aequitashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-scoped debug log retention beyond standard TTL

Samir — thanks for the clear summary. We're able to evaluate and (if approved) implement a tenant-scoped retention exception, but we need to run a short internal review and produce the evidence pack you requested. High-level plan from our side:

1) Compliance will draft a formal exception attestation and list of deliverables.
2) Platform will capture and export redacted sample logs and describe the retention controls (where data resides, access controls, TTL enforcement, and proof-of-delete APIs).
3) Legal/Commercial will confirm whether a DPA amendment or SOW clause is required for the 180-day exception.

Deliverables we propose to send within 3 business days: retention matrix (row per artefact), sample redacted logs (session IDs replaced), a short video walkthrough of the proof-of-delete API, and a signed attestation template.

Can you confirm the minimal set of attestations Aequitas needs to close the review (SOC 2 umbrella evidence vs. CAIQ-specific answers vs. an updated SIG)? That will help us prioritize what to redact and what needs signatures.

I'll loop in Marissa to own evidence production and Jonas for the export and secure-handling playbook.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Security & Privacy Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192
attachments: none

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aequitashealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Aequitas Procurement <procure@aequitashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-scoped debug log retention beyond standard TTL

Samir / Priya — putting forward the evidence list and operational constraints. We can provide the following artifacts scoped to tenant AEQ-237:

- Retention matrix (CSV/PDF): which log classes are retained (request traces, debug stack traces, KV cache snapshots), storage location, retention TTL, responsible owner.
- Sample redacted logs (text file, tokenized): we will replace any PII/PHI and provide a summary of the redaction process.
- Proof-of-delete walkthrough: recorded screencast + API request/response samples (we'll include request IDs and timestamps).
- SIG/CAIQ supplemental answers: a targeted mini-SIG covering retention, deletion, and evidence handling for exceptions.
- Exception attestation: signed by Compliance + SRE describing scope, start/end dates, and mitigation controls (access restrictions, periodic reviews).

Notes / constraints:
- Because AEQ-237 is a single-tenant carveout, we will enable a tenant-tagged retention policy and export a secure, time-limited snapshot to our compliance bucket. For the 180-day period, data will be marked 'retain-exception' and access restricted to a named list of Redwood roles.
- We cannot surface raw system backups; exports will be sanitized and delivered via a secure transfer (Drive folder + DLP controls or an SFTP link).
- For legal reasons we require a signed amendment (DPA addendum) that references the exception period and scope before we flip the retention flag; procurement can run parallel to evidence production.

Planned timeline: initial evidence pack delivered by Wed EOD (3 business days), followed by the attestation + DPA draft within 5 business days. If Aequitas needs a faster cadence, let us know which artifacts are critical.

Attachments: aequitas_retention_matrix.xlsx (stub), sample_redacted_logs.txt (stub), sig_response_draft.docx (draft answers)

Marissa Cole
Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aequitashealth.com>
Cc: Aequitas Procurement <procure@aequitashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-scoped debug log retention beyond standard TTL

Hi all — operations note from the platform side. Technical steps to implement tenant-scoped 180-day debug retention for AEQ-237:

1) Create tenant retention flag (tag: retain-exception:AEQ-237) in the retention service.
2) Emit an immutable audit record for every change (actor, timestamp, rationale). We will include the audit export in the evidence pack.
3) Export sanitized debug traces to a compliance-only bucket every 24 hours; retention policy on that bucket set to 180 days.
4) Implement strict IAM (role-based) on the compliance bucket and provide a temporary service account for Aequitas read-only access if required.
4) Provide a proof-of-delete API endpoint that returns deletion manifests for the compliance bucket when data expires; sample manifest will be included in the pack.

Operational caveat: enabling this flag requires a scheduled maintenance window to ensure no token-cache mismatch during snapshot creation. Estimated 2–3 hours of low-risk maintenance. We'll propose Wed 10pm-1am PT unless you prefer different timing.

I'll add the audit export, the proof-of-delete playbook, and the sanitized sample to the Drive folder and share the link with access controls once the DPA addendum is in flight.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Platform SRE | Redwood Inference
